entries.qa: Reply to it is usually الله معك (al-LAH MA-ak). Lebanese also say باي.
Masculine form (file convention: masculine speaker/listener). A female speaker says آسفة (AAS-feh). سوري (SOR-ree) is also very common in casual speech.
Same word as excuse_me in the vetted file. Also common: ولو (wa-LAW) and أهلا وسهلا.
Neutral agreement. طيب (TAY-yeb) and أوكي are equally common; ماشي is most typical in Palestine/Jordan.

Blank takes number + 'person' (شخص), and the noun changes with the number: لشخص واحد (1), لشخصين (dual, 2), لتلات/لأربع أشخاص (3-10, plural). See examples. Waiters may simply hear the number with fingers.
منيو is the everyday word; formal قائمة الطعام appears in print.
ALLERGY. Literal: 'I have an allergy from ___' (= I'm allergic to ___). حساسية على ___ is also heard. Blank takes the allergen with the article (المكسرات, البيض). Gender-neutral.

Masculine form (file convention: masculine speaker/listener). Female speaker: أنا نباتية (na-baa-TEE-yeh). Literal: 'I am vegetarian'. Note: some people assume chicken/fish are fine; add ما باكل لحمة ولا جاج (I don't eat meat or chicken) if needed.
ALLERGY/DIET. Literal: 'Without ___, please.' Blank takes the noun with no article (بدون لحمة, بدون حليب). بلا (BA-la) ___ is a common alternative.
سفري ('for travel') is the standard takeaway word in Jordan/Palestine/Syria; in Lebanon 'take away' (in English) is common too.
Literal: 'Here, please.' Natural as an answer to هون ولا سفري؟. Fuller: بدي آكل هون (I want to eat here).
Refers to the meal (masc). For a feminine dish (e.g. الأكلة) كانت كتير طيبة. Palestinians also say زاكي (ZAA-kee).
Gender agrees with the item, not the speaker: كمان واحدة (WAH-deh) for feminine items like قهوة or بيرة.
لـ + ال merges to لل (للمطار). Colloquially تكت/تيكت is also heard. Blank takes the destination with its article.
هاد/بيروح assume a masculine vehicle (باص, سرفيس, قطار). For a feminine noun (e.g. السيارة) هاي بتروح. على + ال contracts to عال (عالمطار).

Masculine form (file convention: masculine speaker/listener). Addressed to a male driver; to a female driver وصّليني (was-si-LEE-nee). ودّيني على ___ is also common in Palestine/Jordan. على + ال contracts to عال.
Masculine form (file convention: masculine speaker/listener). Addressed to a male driver; female: وقّفي. نزّلني هون (naz-ZIL-nee hoon, 'let me off here') is equally common.
Literal: 'When does the coming one leave?' Masculine (bus/train). For a feminine noun: إمتى بتطلع الجاية. Jordanian/Palestinian also أيمتى.
Uncertain: rail is rare in the Levant and travellers may not need this; رصيف is the standard word for platform (also 'sidewalk'). Some say أي منصة.
Literal: 'How much time does it need?' Also: قديش بتاخد وقت؟
Colloquial; signs/tickets use ذهاب فقط / ذهاب وإياب.
Direction 'to the left'. شمال also means north; يسار (ya-SAAR) is understood everywhere.
Direction 'to the right'.
Direction. على طول (a-la TOOL) is equally common across the Levant.
Masculine form (file convention: masculine speaker/listener). Female speaker: أنا ضايعة (DAY-'a). Literal: 'I am lost'.
Same form for male and female listener.
Fuller: الحجز باسم ___ (the reservation is under the name ___). Blank takes a name.
Also: شو كلمة السر تبع الواي فاي؟

entries.pronunciation_easy: is-SAA-a ad-DAYSH LAA-zim AT-la min il-GHUR-feh
entries.qa: Literal: 'At what time must I leave the room?' Hotel staff also understand إمتى الـ check out؟. Not fully sure which is more natural at reception; flag for review.
Literal: 'Can I leave the bags here?' (no possessive, more natural).
Verb agrees with the noun's gender: masculine ما بيشتغل, feminine ما بتشتغل. Blank takes the noun with its article. مش شغّال / خربان (broken) are also common.
Towel: منشفة in Palestine/Syria/Lebanon; Jordanians often say بشكير.
عم is Syrian/Lebanese/Palestinian; Jordanians often drop it: بس بتفرّج.
Object pronoun agrees with the item: باخدها (BAAKH-d-ha) for a feminine item.
Adjective agrees with the item: غالية for a feminine item.
Object pronoun agrees with the item: أجرّبها for a feminine item (e.g. جاكيت is masc, بلوزة fem).
Literal: 'Is there another size?' مقاس is also used; for shoes people say نمرة.
كيس = plastic/shopping bag.
Literal: 'I want to cut my hair, please' (the normal way to ask at a barber).
Uncertain: literal 'just a light cut'. Barbers also say ترتيب (tidy-up) or شوي من فوق. Reviewer to confirm most natural.
Uncertain: literal 'the two sides shorter, please'. Alternative: قصّر عالجناب أكتر. Reviewer to confirm barber usage.
Said while showing a photo. Just هيك also works.

Masculine form (file convention: masculine speaker/listener). Addressed to a male barber (female: ظبّطيلي). Literal: 'Fix my beard for me, please.' Not fully sure this is the most common barber phrasing; تحديد دقن is used for shaping.
EMERGENCY. Literal: 'Help me!' (addressed to everyone, plural). Also shouted: الحقوني! (il-Ha-'OO-nee, 'come quickly to me'). Gender-neutral.

EMERGENCY. Literal: 'Call the police!' Masculine form (file convention: masculine speaker/listener). Female listener: اتصلي (it-TSI-lee); to a group: اتصلوا. In Lebanon البوليس is also heard. Police number: 911 in Jordan/Palestine, 112 in Lebanon.
EMERGENCY. Literal: 'I want/need a doctor.' Gender-neutral. محتاج دكتور (masc) / محتاجة (fem) is also used.
EMERGENCY. Literal: 'Where is the pharmacy?'
EMERGENCY. Literal: 'This is an emergency case!' Slightly formal but widely understood; in speech ضروري كتير! ('very urgent') is also used.
EMERGENCY. Literal: 'I lost ___.' The possessive 'my' is a suffix on the noun (-ee), so the word changes: ضيّعت جواز سفري ('I lost my passport'). See examples. Gender-neutral.

EMERGENCY. Literal: 'I'm not feeling myself well.' Masculine form (file convention: masculine speaker/listener). Female speaker: مش حاسة حالي منيح (HAAS-seh). Shorter: أنا تعبان (masc) / تعبانة (fem), 'I'm unwell/tired'.
EMERGENCY. Literal: 'I must call someone.' Gender-neutral.
Plural 'you' (عندكم), the normal way to ask a shop, café or hotel, and gender-neutral. To one person: عندك (IN-dak to a man, IN-dik to a woman). Blank takes the noun with no article.
Blank takes the noun WITH the article (قديش التذكرة؟), where English says 'a'. قديش حق ___ / قديش سعر ___ also common. Jordan/Palestine also بقديش.

Masculine speaker (file convention); a woman says محتاجة (muh-TAA-jeh). Literal: 'I (m.) need ___, please.' بدي ___ ('I want') is often used instead and is gender-neutral. Blank takes the noun with no article.

Literal: 'Is there ___ here near?' قريب used as an adverb so it stays the same for every noun. Not fully sure this is the most natural; 'في ___ قريب من هون؟' is also common but then قريب agrees (قريبة for feminine nouns like صيدلية). Blank takes the noun with no article.

Preposition بـ ('with') is inside the blank because it merges with the article/possessive: بالكرت, بتلفوني; 'cash' is just كاش. فيني matches the vetted pay_card; Jordan/Palestine also بقدر أدفع (BA'-dar). Gender-neutral.
Blank takes a 'you' verb form, which is masculine here (file convention: male listener); to a woman add -ee (تكتبيلي). Matches vetted help_me / say_again / speak_slowly.
Two blanks: the item, then what to leave out, both with no article. Gender-neutral. بلا (BA-la) is a common alternative to بدون.
Blank takes an 'I' verb form (أقعد, أصوّر), which is gender-neutral. Jordan/Palestine also بقدر ___ هون؟ / مسموح ___ هون؟ ('is it allowed').
Gender-neutral. على + ال contracts to عال (عالمدخل), like take_me_to. Jordan/Palestine often بدوّر على (ba-DOW-wir) instead of عم دوّر.

Literal: 'Is ___ within the price?' Chosen because it stays the same for every noun; the vetted tip_included uses محسوبة, which would need to agree (محسوب/محسوبة) with each noun. Blank takes the noun with its article.
Blank takes an 'I' verb form, gender-neutral. منين (min-NAYN, 'from where') is also very natural for buying/getting things: منين بشتري تذاكر؟

PRIORITY REVIEW. To a woman: اتركيني.

Said by a man; a woman: قريبة (a-REE-beh).

entries.qa: To a woman: جابِك (JAA-bek).
The blank holds the whole time or place with its little word ("at seven", "at the station"), because that word changes in most languages.
Only after a 'busy' answer. If the answer was a no, say 'No worries, another time.' instead.
PRIORITY REVIEW (a boundary: a clear, polite no).
PRIORITY REVIEW (a boundary that must stay firm). To a woman: اتركيلي.

Bars and alcohol are not a given everywhere; this set is for places that have them.

can_i_have.target: ممكن تعطيني عصير برتقان، لو سمحت؟
can_i_have.pronunciation_easy: MUM-kin ta-TEE-nee a-SEER bur-ta-AAN, law sa-MAHT

i_would_like.pronunciation_easy: BAD-dee KAA-set na-BEED AB-yad, law sa-MAHT

table_for.qa: Dual form: 'for two persons' is one word, شخصين.
Before a plural noun تلاتة shortens to تلات.
Before a plural noun أربعة shortens to أربع.

allergic_to.qa: ALLERGY. Literal: 'I have an allergy from nuts (mixed nuts)'.
ALLERGY. Literal: 'I have an allergy from peanuts ('Sudanese pistachio'). Lebanese also say فستق عبيد; plain فستق means pistachio, so keep سوداني'.
ALLERGY. Literal: 'I have an allergy from gluten (loanword; staff may not know it, add القمح 'wheat' if needed)'.
ALLERGY. Literal: 'I have an allergy from 'fruits of the sea' = shellfish/seafood; may be taken to include fish. Crustaceans specifically: القشريات'.
ALLERGY. Literal: 'I have an allergy from milk'.
ALLERGY. Literal: 'I have an allergy from eggs'.

without.qa: DIET. Literal: 'Without meat (some cooks don't count chicken as لحمة; add ولا جاج 'nor chicken'), please.'

take_me_to.target: وصّلني على محطة القطار، لو سمحت.
take_me_to.pronunciation_easy: was-SIL-nee A-la ma-HAT-tit il-i-TAAR, law sa-MAHT

take_me_to.target: وصّلني على وسط البلد، لو سمحت.
take_me_to.pronunciation_easy: was-SIL-nee A-la WUST il-BA-lad, law sa-MAHT

doesnt_work.qa: Frame not used literally: 'the hot water doesn't work' is unnatural; Levantine says 'there's no hot water'.
Uncertain: قفل الباب خربان ('the door lock is broken') may be more natural.

lost_my.qa: EMERGENCY. Literal: 'I lost my passport ('my travel permit')'.
EMERGENCY. Literal: 'I lost my phone. Jordan/Palestine also جوالي / موبايلي'.
EMERGENCY. Literal: 'I lost my wallet. محفظتي also understood'.
EMERGENCY. Literal: 'I lost my room key ('key of my room')'.

how_much_is.qa: Literal: 'How much is the coffee?' Natural way to ask the price of one coffee.
For a per-night price: قديش الغرفة بالليلة؟

i_need.qa: SAFETY. Literal: 'I (m.) need help, please.' Woman: محتاجة مساعدة. In a real emergency people shout ساعدوني! (sa-a-DOO-nee, 'help me!').
Woman: محتاجة. بدي مي is just as natural.
Woman: محتاجة. بدي تاكسي ('I want a taxi') is the more everyday phrasing.

is_there_nearby.qa: تواليت (twa-LEET) is also widely used for a public toilet.

pay_with.qa: Literal: 'Can I pay with my phone?' Contactless phone payment may not be accepted in smaller shops.

can_you.qa: Literal: 'Can you write it for me, please?' Masculine (male listener); to a woman تكتبيلي ياه. Palestine/Jordan also تكتبهولي.

like_without.target: بدي قهوة بدون حليب، لو سمحت.
like_without.pronunciation_easy: BAD-dee AH-weh bi-DOON ha-LEEB, law sa-MAHT
like_without.qa: Plain قهوة usually means Arabic coffee, which never has milk; this makes most sense for نسكافيه / قهوة أمريكية.

like_without.target: بدي شاي بدون سكر، لو سمحت.
like_without.pronunciation_easy: BAD-dee shaay bi-DOON SUK-kar, law sa-MAHT
like_without.qa: Tea is served very sweet by default, so this is worth saying. سادة (SAA-deh, 'plain') also means no sugar.

like_without.target: بدي مي بدون تلج، لو سمحت.
like_without.pronunciation_easy: BAD-dee may bi-DOON talj, law sa-MAHT

can_i_here.qa: Literal: 'Can I park the car here?' أصفّ written colloquially as صفّ after فيني. Lebanon also أركن (ER-kon).
Literal: 'Can I photograph here?' (أصوّر, colloquially صوّر).

looking_for.qa: Literal: 'I'm looking for the hotel of mine.' فندقي (FUN-du-'ee) also correct but less colloquial.

is_included.qa: Hotels also: الفطور مع الغرفة؟ ('Is breakfast with the room?').
For a flight/bus ticket people may say الشنطة مع التذكرة؟ ('Is the bag with the ticket?').

where_can_i.qa: Literal: 'Where can I find a taxi?' (the usual way to say 'get' one).
Literal: 'Where can I change money?' مصاري = money; فلوس (floos) also common in Jordan.
شريحة = SIM card; سيم كارد also understood.

anything_else.qa: Said to a male customer; to a female: بدِك (BID-dek). Palestinians/Jordanians also say إشي (ISH-ee) for شي.

here_you_go.qa: To a male customer; to a female: تفضّلي (taf-DAL-ee).

how_many_people.qa: Also heard: قديش واحد؟ / كم واحد؟

have_booking.qa: To a male guest; to a female: عندِك (AN-dek).

this_way.qa: Often تفضّل من هون (please, this way).

next_stop.qa: Spoken form; recorded announcements use formal المحطة القادمة.

its_closed.qa: Agrees with the place: مسكّرة (m-sak-KA-ra) for a feminine noun like الصيدلية.

receipt_question.qa: To a male customer; female: بدِك. Jordan/Palestine also say الوصل (il-WASL) for receipt.

how_would_you_like_it.qa: Literal: 'How do you want the cut?' To a male customer (barber context).

sorry_i_cant.qa: Said by a woman. A man: آسف (AA-sef).

seeing_someone.qa: Said by a woman. A man: مرتبط (mir-TIBet).

thats_altogether.qa: A price heard at a till, with a plain number so it fits any currency.

l2_within_days.qa: Reviewer: confirm أربعطعشر for fourteen in this dialect.

l2_busy_weekend.qa: Said by a woman. A man: مشغول (mash-GHOOL).

l2_boarding_closes.target: الصعود للطيارة بيسكّر بعد عشرين دقيقة.
l2_boarding_closes.pronunciation_easy: is-su-OOD lat-tay-YAA-ra bi-SAK-ker ba'd ish-REEN da-EE-a
